regulation.name: Regulation Set M-C
regulation.start_note: Live 8 Sep 2026 7:00 PM PDT — 1 Dec 2026 5:59 PM PST

formats.name: Doubles
formats.note: The official VGC format. Register 6, select 4 at team preview.

formats.name: Singles
formats.note: Separate ranked ladder with its own rating.

rules.gimmick: One per battle — Terastallize OR Mega Evolve, never both.

items.name: Leek
items.effect: Raises the critical-hit ratio of Farfetch'd or Sirfetch'd by 2 stages.
items.note: With Focus Energy or Dire Claw-style boosts, Sirfetch'd crits on demand — ignores enemy Defense boosts and Intimidate.

items.name: Rocky Helmet
items.effect: Attacker takes 1/6 of its max HP when it hits the holder with a contact move.
items.note: The single most important M-C item. Mega Golisopod and Mega Lucario Z are contact-locked; Rocky Helmet punishes both.

items.name: Air Balloon
items.effect: Holder is immune to Ground moves until it is hit by any damaging move, which pops the balloon.
items.note: Blanks Earthquake from Garchomp and Mega Garchomp Z, and lets a partner click spread Ground freely.

items.name: Red Card
items.effect: When the holder is hit by a damaging move, the attacker is switched out at random. Consumed.
items.note: Undoes a setup sweep and drags Megas out of position.

items.name: Eject Button
items.effect: When the holder is hit by a damaging move, it switches out immediately. Consumed.
items.note: Pivot out of an Intimidate cycle or a trapped matchup for free.

items.name: Binding Band
items.effect: Increases damage from binding moves (Whirlpool, Fire Spin, Infestation) to 1/6 per turn.
items.note: Niche, but a real win condition on trapping cores in singles.

items.name: Normal Gem
items.effect: Boosts the power of a Normal-type move by 30%. Consumed on use.
items.note: Sharp with Aerilate — Mega Salamence's Normal moves convert to Flying but still consume the Gem, stacking both boosts on Double-Edge.

items.name: Terrain Extender
items.effect: Terrain set by the holder lasts 8 turns instead of 5.
items.note: Turns a 5-turn terrain window into effectively the whole game.

items.name: Electric Seed
items.effect: Raises Defense by 1 stage on Electric Terrain. Consumed.

items.name: Grassy Seed
items.effect: Raises Defense by 1 stage on Grassy Terrain. Consumed.

items.name: Psychic Seed
items.effect: Raises Sp. Def by 1 stage on Psychic Terrain. Consumed.

items.name: Misty Seed
items.effect: Raises Sp. Def by 1 stage on Misty Terrain. Consumed.
items.note: The only Misty setter in the pool is a Tapu-less field move, so this is the weakest of the four.

items.name: Choice Scarf
items.effect: Raises Speed by 50% but locks the holder into the first move it uses.

items.name: Choice Band
items.effect: Raises Attack by 50% but locks the holder into the first move it uses.

items.name: Choice Specs
items.effect: Raises Sp. Atk by 50% but locks the holder into the first move it uses.

items.name: Life Orb
items.effect: Raises damage by 30%; holder loses 10% of max HP per damaging move.

items.name: Focus Sash
items.effect: Survives a KO from full HP with 1 HP. Consumed.

items.name: Assault Vest
items.effect: Raises Sp. Def by 50% but prevents the use of status moves.

items.name: Leftovers
items.effect: Restores 1/16 of max HP at the end of each turn.

items.name: Sitrus Berry
items.effect: Restores 25% of max HP when the holder drops below 50%. Consumed.

items.name: Safety Goggles
items.effect: Immune to powder moves and to weather chip damage.

items.name: Covert Cloak
items.effect: Protects the holder from the secondary effects of moves.
items.note: Blanks Rock Slide flinches and Fake Out.

items.name: Clear Amulet
items.effect: Prevents the holder's stats from being lowered by other Pokémon.
items.note: The premier Intimidate answer for a physical Mega.

items.name: Mental Herb
items.effect: Cures Taunt, Encore, Torment, Attract and Disable. Consumed.

items.name: Weakness Policy
items.effect: Raises Attack and Sp. Atk by 2 stages when hit by a super-effective move. Consumed.

items.name: Expert Belt
items.effect: Raises the power of super-effective moves by 20%.

items.name: Wide Lens
items.effect: Raises accuracy by 10%.

items.name: Loaded Dice
items.effect: Multi-hit moves always hit 4-5 times.

items.name: Booster Energy
items.effect: Activates Protosynthesis or Quark Drive. Consumed.

items.name: Eviolite
items.effect: Raises Defense and Sp. Def by 50% for a Pokémon that can still evolve.

items.name: Light Clay
items.effect: Extends Reflect and Light Screen to 8 turns.

items.name: Throat Spray
items.effect: Raises Sp. Atk by 1 stage after using a sound move. Consumed.

usage.name: Garchomp
usage.why: Earthquake plus Rock Slide is the best spread-damage pairing in the format, and it now has a Mega Z form that flips it to a special sweeper.

usage.name: Basculegion
usage.why: Last Respects scales with your own fainted Pokémon and appeared on over 99% of tournament sets. The single highest-usage Pokémon of M-A.

usage.name: Kingambit
usage.why: Supreme Overlord plus priority Sucker Punch closes games. Defiant punishes Intimidate.

usage.name: Whimsicott
usage.why: Prankster Tailwind is the format's default speed control, with 68% co-usage alongside Garchomp.

usage.name: Sinistcha
usage.why: Hospitality plus Rage Powder soaks up a turn every game and heals its partner.

usage.name: Mega Metagross
usage.why: The best raw stat line of M-B: 145 Attack alongside 110 Speed and Tough Claws.

usage.name: Mega Mawile
usage.why: Huge Power doubles Attack to an effective 525. Gholdengo plus Mega Mawile is the format's safest core.

usage.name: Mega Charizard Y
usage.why: Drought plus Heat Wave, and its Flying typing means a Garchomp partner can click Earthquake freely — that pair was on 23.9% of all M-A teams.

usage.name: Gholdengo
usage.why: Good as Gold blanks every status move in the format, including Intimidate-adjacent support.

usage.name: Incineroar
usage.why: Intimidate plus Fake Out remains the safest support pick in doubles.

usage.name: Mega Swampert
usage.why: Swift Swim under rain outruns the entire unboosted format.

usage.name: Mega Staraptor
usage.why: Contrary turns Close Combat's drops into boosts, so it snowballs defensively while attacking.

usage.name: Sneasler
usage.why: Unburden plus Dire Claw's status chance makes it a nightmare once it is airborne.

usage.name: Amoonguss
usage.why: Spore is still the only sleep move worth the slot, and Rage Powder buys turns.

usage.name: Annihilape
usage.why: Rage Fist grows every time it is hit, which doubles punishes spread moves.

usage.name: Pelipper
usage.why: Drizzle plus Tailwind, and the enabler for Mega Swampert.

usage.name: Farigiraf
usage.why: Armor Tail shuts off every priority move in the format, protecting a Trick Room turn.

usage.name: Ursaluna
usage.why: Guts Facade under Trick Room is the hardest single hit available to a non-Mega.

usage.name: Mega Salamence
usage.why: 700 BST with 120 Speed and Aerilate Double-Edge. A two-time World Champion Mega returning into a format with no Steel-heavy top tier.

usage.name: Mega Garchomp Z
usage.why: 151 Speed and 141 Sp. Atk on a pure-Dragon body with Levitate. It outspeeds the entire format and ignores Ground moves, Spikes and terrain.

usage.name: Mega Lucario Z
usage.why: 164 Sp. Atk at 151 Speed, and Aura Guard halves incoming contact damage — offense and defense in one slot.

usage.name: Mega Golisopod
usage.why: Bug/Steel with 175 Defense and 150 Attack, Tough Claws, and 40 Speed that begs for Trick Room. First Impression at +30% is a genuine opening threat.

usage.name: Mega Baxcalibur
usage.why: 175 Attack and 115 HP, and Thermal Exchange makes it burn-proof and turns Fire coverage into a free Attack boost.

usage.name: Mega Absol Z
usage.why: Sharpness gives 50% on every slicing move, but frail defenses keep it out of the top tier.

usage.name: Rillaboom
usage.why: Grassy Surge plus priority Grassy Glide, and Grassy Terrain halves Earthquake — a direct structural answer to the Garchomp cores.

usage.name: Indeedee-F
usage.why: Psychic Surge blocks all priority — it turns off Sucker Punch, Fake Out, Grassy Glide and Aqua Jet at once, and Follow Me protects a Trick Room setter.

usage.name: Cinderace
usage.why: Libero gives it a free STAB on anything, and base 119 Speed sits above most of the format.

usage.name: Pincurchin
usage.why: The only Electric Surge in the pool. Slow and frail, but Electric Terrain blocks sleep and doubles Rising Voltage.

notes.headline: M-C is a speed-tier reset and a terrain format waiting to happen.

threads.title: The 151 Speed ceiling
threads.body: Mega Garchomp Z and Mega Lucario Z both sit at base 151 Speed, well above the base 120 Mega Salamence and the old 110 Mega Metagross benchmark. Every Speed number you learned in M-B is now one tier too low. Either invest to outrun 151, or stop trying and go under them with Trick Room.

threads.title: Terrain arrived fully assembled
threads.body: M-C added Rillaboom (Grassy Surge), Indeedee (Psychic Surge) and Pincurchin (Electric Surge) in the same patch as Terrain Extender and all four Seeds. That is not a coincidence. Grassy Terrain halving Earthquake and Psychic Terrain blocking priority both attack the exact cores that defined M-B.

threads.title: Contact is a liability again
threads.body: Mega Golisopod, Mega Lucario Z, Mega Metagross and Mega Mawile all want to click contact moves. Rocky Helmet arrived in the same regulation. A single Rocky Helmet holder taxes four of the top Megas 1/6 per hit.

threads.title: Priority is contested
threads.body: Kingambit's Sucker Punch and Basculegion's Aqua Jet defined M-B endgames. Indeedee's Psychic Terrain turns both off outright, and Rillaboom's Grassy Glide jumps the queue. Whoever controls the terrain controls the last turn.

threads.title: Steel is suddenly crowded
threads.body: Mega Golisopod is Bug/Steel and Mega Lucario Z is Fighting/Steel, joining Mega Metagross, Mega Mawile, Gholdengo and Kingambit. Fire and Ground coverage is at a premium, and Mega Salamence's Aerilate Double-Edge is resisted by more of the field than its raw numbers suggest.

anti_meta.title: Rocky Helmet on a bulky redirector
anti_meta.body: Sinistcha or Amoonguss holding Rocky Helmet punishes Mega Golisopod's First Impression, Mega Metagross's Iron Head and Mega Mawile's Play Rough while still soaking a turn with Rage Powder.

anti_meta.title: Grassy Terrain over Garchomp cores
anti_meta.body: Rillaboom with Terrain Extender halves Earthquake for eight turns. Garchomp was the most-used Pokémon in both M-A and M-B; taxing its best move by 50% for the whole game is the highest-leverage structural choice in M-C.

anti_meta.title: Trick Room under the 151s
anti_meta.body: Mega Golisopod at 40 Speed with 175 Defense is a natural Trick Room abuser, and Farigiraf's Armor Tail protects the setup turn from every priority move. The two fastest Megas in the format become the two slowest.

anti_meta.title: Air Balloon on a Steel Mega
anti_meta.body: Mega Metagross or Mega Mawile with Air Balloon flips the Ground matchup that normally checks them, and lets your own Garchomp click Earthquake without clipping your partner.

anti_meta.title: Clear Amulet on your Mega
anti_meta.body: Intimidate from Incineroar is the cheapest way to blunt a physical Mega. Clear Amulet costs you a damage item but guarantees your Mega Salamence or Mega Baxcalibur hits at full Attack all game.
